title: Bob's bit of the dual sample equals Alice's reversed bit
statement: Let $\omega$ be a sample of the hard distribution over $n$ coordinates, and write $\mathrm{rev}(i) = n-1-i$ for the reversal of a coordinate $i \in \{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$. Form the dual sample by swapping Alice's and Bob's roles and reversing the coordinate order. Then Bob's bit at coordinate $i$ of the dual sample equals Alice's bit at the reversed coordinate $\mathrm{rev}(i)$ of the original sample.
hypotheses_covered: a hard-distribution sample ω over n coordinates
a coordinate index i in Fin n
replaced: Bob's bit in the dual hard sample is Alice's original bit at the reversed coordinate.
